chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from one of the people of Ahvaz, from Al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

'There is a vein in the body called Al-Asha (Dinner). So if a man neglects the dinner, that vein does not cease supplicating against him until morning, saying: "May Allah keep you hungry as you kept me hungry, and may Allah keep you thirsty as you kept me thirsty." Therefore, let not one of you neglect the dinner, even if it is a morsel of bread or a drink of water.'.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of not skipping dinner according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Rida (peace be upon him) identifies a specific vein called 'Al-Isha' (evening) within the body that supplicates for hunger and thirst upon the one who neglects the evening meal, linking physical sustenance to spiritual well-being. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining regular nourishment as a means of preserving health and avoiding the 'complaint' of the body's parts, encouraging even minimal intake like a bite of bread or sip of water to fulfill this bodily right.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin ZIyad, from one of the people of Ahvaaz, 
(It has been narrated) from Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There are veins in the body called A’ Asha. So if the man neglects the dinner, that vein does not cease supplicating against him till the morning, saying, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you hungry as you kept me hungry, and may Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you thirsty as you kept me thirsty’. Therefore, not one of you should neglect the dinner even though it may be a morsel of bread, or a drink of water’.
en.sarwar: 12. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from certain persons of Ahwaz who has said the following: “Al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

In the body there is a vein called ‘Isha’. If one does not take dinner, it continues praying against him until morning; and it says, ‘May Allah make you hungry just as you kept me hungry, and may Allah make you thirsty just as you kept me thirsty.’ No one of you must neglect taking dinner, even if it is one morsel of bread or a sip of water.’”
